What follows is the search-result snippet, which quotes the article's own words from an approved domain.
Per the brief's Rule 1 this is an acceptable source; it is recorded here verbatim rather than paraphrased.

"Under Mr Burnham's new policy, the state pension will continue to rise by the highest of inflation or
2.5pc. Earnings growth will remain a consideration, but only to maintain pensions at an as-yet-undeclared
percentage of the national average wage.

The Resolution Foundation has spent years making the case for a very similar policy, using a so-called
'smooth earnings link', to replace the triple lock, which it described as 'unsustainable'. In fact, Mr
Bell himself co-authored a paper in which he described the current mechanism as a 'messy tool for raising
pensions' and called for permanent change.

He also said the Government should set a clear objective for the level of state pension relative to the
average worker's pay. This too will be a feature under Mr Burnham's policy and, according to officials
from the Department for Work and Pensions, it will be at least 30pc."

WHAT IT SUPPORTS IN THE BRIEF:
- That the replacement mechanism keeps the earnings element only as a floor expressed as a share of
  average earnings, which DWP officials put at no less than 30%.
- That the design closely follows the Resolution Foundation's long-argued "smooth earnings link".
NOTE FOR THE COPY: the Telegraph describes the percentage as "as-yet-undeclared" in one sentence and
reports officials putting it at "at least 30pc" in another. The brief therefore says officials put it at
no less than 30%, and does not present the figure as a settled published target.
